note: Every site in src/ where the code could decide which record a text names, found by mechanism: partial (includes, startsWith, endsWith, indexOf, search, match, test, exec, a replace by a built pattern, any split, a Set or Map lookup inside a scan), whole (=== between two texts inside a list scan, one of them a name), whole-single (the same outside a scan), keyed (a Map, Set or object read by a name), bypass (a carried item's own name handed to a function, where the row it names may be meant), fallback (a lookup's miss replaced by another record: ?? list[0], ?? other.find(...)), first (a returned list's first element taken as the record), normalizer (a function folding text by its own toLowerCase), number (a number read from text), switch, sql, collator, and helper (a call, with two texts, of a src function that matches a part of one in the other, such as containsPhrase). scripts/test-name-lookups.mjs holds each file's sites, per mechanism, to these counts. The rule: when a text decides which record or row a thing is and an engine then applies that record's rules or state (identity), it is compared by textKey as the whole name, after only a "+N" bonus, a bracket note, a leading article of the table language or a "Prefix:" of ODM's own feature names is stripped, or it names the row in a field (srdName, slug, id); a miss is refused with the options listed, never a record holding a word of it, the first one or a default. Search (retrieval, safety lines, names in prose, filter boxes) may match words, since a miss costs nothing. A new site is one of these, classified here with its reason.

classes.identity: decides which record a text names, by the whole name through textKey (or a field naming the row); a miss is refused with the options
classes.search: a finder where a partial hit is the point and a miss costs nothing: retrieval, safety lines, names in prose, filter boxes, shortlists
classes.key: ids, slugs, paths, protocol, model ids, stored forms and ODM's own English keys compared as stored
classes.parse: cutting or testing text that names no record: formats, dice, stat-block and rules text
classes.pattern: a fixed pattern over text that reads no record's name
classes.authoring: the workshop's and WorldForge's authoring tools, which read what an author writes as they go
